classification.difficultyReason: Combine equilateral-triangle geometry with equal circular arcs and sectors, then account for overlapping triangle areas to find the enclosed area exactly.

content.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is equilateral with side length $2\text{ cm}$. Circular arcs $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$ have centres $C$, $A$ and $B$ respectively. Answer each part in exact form.

spec.description: Unshaded equilateral triangle with three outward circular arcs. A is above B and C; filled points P, Q and R lie on the left, bottom and right arcs respectively. All straight triangle sides remain visible.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CA=2 cm. Arc APB has centre C, arc BQC has centre A, and arc CRA has centre B; each subtends pi/3 radians. The boundary order is A-P-B-Q-C-R-A.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source geometry, labels and the three supplied arc points are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the length of the arc $AB$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of the sector $CAPBC$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the length of the perimeter $APBQCRA$.

answer.worked:
The boundary consists of three equal arcs.
$$\begin{align*}P&=3\times\frac{2\pi}{3}\\P&=2\pi\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the area of $\triangle ABC$ and hence find the area enclosed by the perimeter $APBQCRA$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\triangle ABC}&=\frac12\times2\times2\sin60^\circ\\A_{\triangle ABC}&=\sqrt3\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
Each curved segment is a sector minus $\triangle ABC$. The enclosed region consists of the triangle and three such segments.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{enclosed}}&=\sqrt3+3\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}-\sqrt3\right)\\A_{\text{enclosed}}&=2\pi-2\sqrt3\\A_{\text{enclosed}}&=2(\pi-\sqrt3)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
